title: Teddy Hill's band after Roy left: trumpets, reeds, trombones
summary: Clarke names the trumpeters (Dizzy, Al Killian, Joe Guy), reeds and trombonists in Teddy Hill's band, including Henry Wood who got him fired, and fails to recall the pianist and bassist.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: All right, let's go back a minute. Well, so at that time you were -- when Webb was playing the Savoy then and you were with Teddy Hill.
Well, Roy was with Teddy, though, for a time.
Yeah. This was after. Because Roy had
And Diz had come in his place?
Diz, and then we had Al Killian.
Those were the three trumpet players.
Yeah, I do remember that, yeah.
Well, Joe Guy, I mean he had the same kind of ideas.
Did Al Killian? I remember Al --
He wasn't much with solos. songs. He was kind of a Cat Anderson, you know.
At the time. He was the high note man.
Well, I remember he -- when T-bone was big on the West Coast, Al Killian made records with T-Bone then.
So I guess -- I guess, you know, he must have come out. Was he Texas or something?
I don't know. Maybe he was Texas. Maybe he was.
Yeah. I think that's what he was, yeah. Well, so -- but you say -- so it wasn't the brass section that, you know, felt that you weren't giving them the framework that you were used to.
Well, let me see. We changed quite a bit the reed section. We had Big Bob Carroll. You remember Bob Carroll?
Wasn't he with Redman one time?
We had Bob and another tenor player named Hanpire (PHONETIC), Henry Hanpire. He was from Pittsburgh.
And -- who was the alto player.
Who was in that rhythm section with you? Who was the piano player?
That was -- who was the piano player? Wasn't it --
I don't -- was it with Sonny White?
No, it wasn't Sonny White. No. But the bass player was the old fellow who played. Oh, you know.
Never mind. I'll remind you tomorrow.
But I can see his face just as clear.
Yeah. Well, anyway, that's -- we've really named the people in Teddy Hill's band who stood out.
And Eli Robinson was a very good trombone player.
Yeah, I remember him. He'd been working with Buddy.
And we had Jimmy Wood's brother, Henry Wood, a trombone player, too.
He's the one who had me fired.
And I worked a lot with his nephew, Jimmy Wood, who was the bass player with Duke for a long time.
So I'm always telling him about his sad uncle.
